name: Whose Eyes?
description: Gather the people a topic touches, then step inside a classmate's suggested viewpoint. No scores.
when: When a topic has more sides than the discussion is hearing, and you want thirty viewpoints instead of five.
playTime: ~15–20 min (scales with class size, the circle reads every voice)

viewpoints: A parent working two jobs who gets home at eight
The substitute teacher who has to collect it
A student who plays two sports and gets home at seven
A younger sibling who wants to play but has to be quiet
The teacher who grades it all on Sunday
A student who does not have wifi at home
The family dog waiting for a walk
A college admissions officer reading transcripts

lines: Homework is the one thing I cannot help with. I am asleep when it gets done.
I worry my kid thinks I do not care. I hope the school knows I do.
Does anyone at school know what time I get home?
I hand out the worksheet and half the room did not do it. I have no idea who is struggling.
I worry about wasting a whole period on something the real teacher will redo.
Is there a version of this that works without me knowing the class?
I start homework at nine after practice and dinner. Everything takes twice as long when you are tired.
I worry that I will have to quit a sport to keep my grades. I hope there is another way.
Why does every class assume they are the only one giving homework?
My big sister used to build forts with me. Now she says "later" and later never comes.
I worry she is always stressed. I hope she gets a break soon.
Why do they need her all evening when they already had her all day?
I assign it because I want to know who is lost before the test. Then I lose my Sunday to it.
I worry the kids who copied learned nothing and the kids who struggled gave up.
Is there a faster way to find out who needs help?
I do the reading on my phone in the parking lot of the library. Online homework is the worst.
I worry the teacher thinks I am lazy. I hope someone asks why it is late.
Could there be a version that works on paper?
Nobody has time for the park anymore. The leash has not moved since Tuesday.
I worry my person is always at the desk. I hope the weekend is different.
Does the homework get done faster if you take a walk first?
I see a transcript, not the evenings behind it. Grades from homework blur what a student actually knows.
I worry we reward compliance over learning. I hope the grade means something.
Which of these grades came from understanding, and which from just turning it in?

intro.message:
WHOSE EYES?

Today's topic: our school's homework policy.

First, name someone, or something, this topic touches. Then a classmate's suggestion will appear on your screen, and you'll look through THEIR eyes.

viewpoints.prompt: Name ONE person, creature, or thing affected by our school's homework policy. Anyone whose eyes we could look through, a substitute teacher? a parent at dinner? the kitchen table it gets done on?

fields.label: From this viewpoint, I worry about or hope for...
A question I have, from here...

circle.message: The circle of voices, one pair of eyes at a time.

end.message: That's the circle. Thirty pairs of eyes, and the question column is tomorrow's lesson. Edit the topic to use this on anything.
